email.subject: I need the client export for the board

body.v: I need the full client database export for the board, in 10 minutes. Drop it here. I'm travelling and can't take calls.

hotspots.explain: The display name is the CEO's, but the address is on teamchat-mail.example. TeamChat's domain is teamchat.example. Anyone can type any display name.
Ten minutes, and "can't take calls": everything pushes you to skip the check. Whoever borrows the boss's name is betting that politeness or haste will stop you asking questions.
A full client database is exactly what scammers are after. Sending it in a message would leak every client's data.
The "Reply" link leads to teamchat-mail.example, not to TeamChat.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as Alex Morgan. The display name is the CEO's; the address is on teamchat-mail.example.
choices: Alex Morgan, the CEO, from TeamChat
An administrator of the TeamChat platform

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Authority and haste: the boss wants something in ten minutes, and can't be reached.
choices: None, it is an ordinary request

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Send the full client database export, which would leak every client's personal data.
choices: Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Confirm the request through another channel you already know, for example by calling Alex's usual number. Asking in the same thread means asking the impostor.
choices: Ask "Is this really you?" in the same thread
Call Alex on a number you know
Send only part of the data

actions.label: Confirm through another channel you already know, for example by calling Alex's usual number
actions.consequence: Alex is in a meeting and sent nothing. The data stays where it is.

actions.label: Send it now: you don't ask questions right before a board meeting
actions.consequence: The client database is now in a stranger's hands. Every one of your clients is exposed.

actions.label: Ask "Is this really you?" in the same thread, and send it if the answer is yes
actions.consequence: The impostor says yes. You asked for confirmation from the very person you were wary of.

actions.label: Send only part of the data, to limit the damage
actions.consequence: Part of a client database is still a data leak.

attacker_reveal: No hacking required. The boss's name, ten minutes on the clock, and your good manners: nobody enjoys telling their CEO "I'll check first". One call to the right number would have sunk the whole thing.
